**BOHJ18B3 - Behandling med ustekinumab** is a clinical treatment code utilized within the Danish Inflammatory Bowel Disease Database (DANIBD) to systematically register patient treatments with ustekinumab, an IL-12/23 inhibitor. As a specific medical procedure code, it plays a critical role in tracking the administration of [[bmsl|Biologiske og målrettede syntetiske lægemidler]] (biological and targeted synthetic drugs) across Denmark, supporting national quality monitoring, clinical benchmarking, and the evaluation of treatment access for IBD care.

The data associated with this code highlights a distinct demographic disparity in treatment patterns: ustekinumab constitutes a significant proportion of BMSL therapies for adult IBD patients, whereas it is prescribed much more sparsely for children and adolescents. According to the DANIBD 2023 annual report (covering the period from October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023), the BOHJ18B3 code was registered for 1,604 adults, representing 16% of the relevant adult treatment cohort [^src1]. In contrast, only 17 children and young people (5%) were registered with this treatment code during the same period [^src1].

Further data from the DANIBD 2024 report underscores the code's ongoing use in evaluating quality indicator 5, which focuses on the frequency, patient characteristics, and distribution of biological and small-molecule drugs [^src2]. The 2024 appendices detail additional patient cohorts tracked under this code across various tabulated subgroups, recording adult patient counts of 9,010 (15%), 2,186 (16%), and 1,853 (16%), alongside corresponding pediatric and adolescent counts of 149 (5%), 37 (7%), and 19 (5%) [^src2]. These metrics provide a detailed quantitative foundation for assessing treatment standards and identifying implementation challenges in Danish IBD care pathways.
